title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 56
paragraphs: When Xerxes had crossed over into Europe, he watched the army crossing under the whip; his army crossed in seven days and seven nights of unbroken passage. Then, it is said, after Xerxes had crossed the Hellespont, a man of that coast exclaimed: “Why, O Zeus, in the likeness of a Persian man and taking for yourself the name Xerxes instead of Zeus, are you proposing to ravage Greece, taking all the nations of men with you? You could have done this without their help.”
